title: Orange County Mayor (runoff)
what_it_does: The county mayor is the county's chief executive: proposes the budget, oversees county departments and staff, and presides over the Board of County Commissioners.
verified_ballot_note: Runoff lineup and Aug. 18 results from WFTV, Central Florida Public Media (https://www.cfpublic.org/politics/2026-08-18/moore-russell-messina-orange-county-mayor-november-runoff) and Spectrum News 13. Nonpartisan.

candidates.name: Tiffany Moore Russell
candidates.photo_source: Ballotpedia candidate photo (downloaded copy in assets/photos)
candidates.background: Orange County Clerk of Courts. Finished first in the four-way Aug. 18 nonpartisan primary.
candidates.primary_result: First in Aug 18 primary with 32% (53,009 votes)

taxes.summary: No public position found as of Sept 2026.

property_tax.summary: At the Orange County mayoral runoff forum in Apopka she said she intends to vote against the November state property-tax amendment, citing the difficulty of replacing the lost revenue and the effect on first responders and smaller municipalities.
property_tax.quote: I do plan to vote no

other_issues.title: Convention center / hotel tax
other_issues.summary: Both runoff candidates expressed hesitancy about expanding the Orange County Convention Center and about using additional hotel-tax money for it; Moore Russell also proposed renovating older apartment complexes in Holden Heights and Pine Hills.

other_issues.title: Budget and transit (Spectrum News 13 debate)
other_issues.summary: In the Spectrum News 13 debate, said she would look at consolidating departments, freezing some hiring and timing capital projects, and favors a more connected rail system including seven-day SunRail service.

sources.title: Orange County mayoral candidates debate the budget, Amendment 3, and affordability in Spectrum News debate (Spectrum News 13)

other_issues.title: Data centers
other_issues.summary: In an Oct. 2026 News 6 interview, Moore Russell said she does not support the large AI data centers being proposed, citing water use, power demand and water quality, and said she commended the county for seeking a moratorium. Quote: "But I do not support the big data centers, the AI data centers that is being proposed today."

sources.title: Orange County mayoral candidates share concerns about large AI data centers (WKMG News 6)

other_issues.title: Jobs and economic development
other_issues.summary: In a News 6 interview, Moore Russell said the county should provide more incentives to attract businesses, called county permitting an impediment for those who want to invest, and said the county should keep investing in CareerSource and trades training.

sources.title: Orange County mayoral candidates pitch plans to bring high-paying jobs (WKMG News 6)

candidates.name: Chris Messina
candidates.photo_source: Ballotpedia candidate photo (downloaded copy in assets/photos)
candidates.background: Tech entrepreneur. Finished second in the four-way primary ahead of former U.S. Rep. Stephanie Murphy (26%) and Commissioner Mayra Uribe (15%).
candidates.primary_result: Second in Aug 18 primary with 28% (45,882 votes)

taxes.summary: Pledges to cut about $200 million a year in county programs through audits and zero-based budgeting so the county can invest without raising taxes, and possibly while cutting them.
taxes.quote: We’ll utilize a forensic audit team, zero-based budgeting, and fiscal discipline to cut $200M/ year in programs which are unnecessary, inefficient, or both.

sources.title: 2026 Voter's Guide - Orange County Mayor runoff (News 6 / News Collaborative of Central Florida)

property_tax.summary: At the Orange County mayoral runoff forum in Apopka he said he supports the November state property-tax amendment, arguing county government can reduce costs while maintaining public safety and that a fire millage increase could cover any shortfall.

other_issues.title: Data centers
other_issues.summary: In an Oct. 2026 News 6 interview, Messina said small data centers are needed but hyperscale data centers are not right for Florida, citing water impact; he suggested data centers make their own energy and said he likes the idea of putting them in space. Quote: "It's the hyperscale data centers, the ones that are football fields in size, those I don't feel are right for Florida."
